title: SKILL.PNG: Learning Agent Skills in Pixel Space
abstract: arXiv:2611.26296v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI agents are commonly specialized for new tasks and domains using skills, i.e. natural language instructions placed in their context. However, the discrete nature of textual skills prevents continuous optimization. Gradient-based approaches such as finetuning, on the other hand, are typically model-specific, preventing skill transfer across different agents. Since many agents today are built on vision-language models (VLMs), we can address these limitations by introducing Skill.png: a method for obtaining skill-like image inputs whose pixels are optimized with gradient descent through the vision encoder of a frozen VLM. Image skills are compatible with any VLM, and a single image can be optimized jointly for an ensemble of models. We show that Skill.png significantly outperforms state-of-the-art textual skills optimized using frontier LLMs in 9 of 16 settings (across 4 VLMs and 4 benchmarks) while requiring only 64 to 256 image tokens i

translated_title: SKILL.PNG：在像素空间中学习智能体技能
translated_abstract: AI智能体通常使用技能（即置于其上下文中的自然语言指令）来针对新任务和新领域进行专门化。然而，文本技能的离散特性阻碍了连续优化。另一方面，基于梯度的方法（如微调）通常是模型特定的，导致技能无法在不同智能体之间迁移。鉴于当今许多智能体都构建在视觉语言模型（VLM）之上，我们可以通过引入Skill.png来克服这些限制：这是一种获取类技能图像输入的方法，其像素通过冻结的VLM视觉编码器使用梯度下降进行优化。图像技能与任何VLM兼容，并且单张图像可以针对模型集合进行联合优化。我们证明，Skill.png在16个设置中的9个（涵盖4个VLM和4个基准测试）中显著优于使用前沿LLM优化的最先进文本技能，同时仅需64到256个图像token。
tldr: 提出Skill.png方法，通过梯度下降优化图像像素来学习可跨VLM通用迁移的智能体技能，在大多数基准设置中超越最先进的文本技能，且token开销极低。
en_tdlr: Skill.png learns transferable agent skills by optimizing image pixels via gradient descent through frozen VLM vision encoders, outperforming state-of-the-art textual skills in 9 of 16 settings while using only 64 to 256 image tokens.
